questions.question_text: Which Azure resource defines a subnet?
questions.explanation: A subnet is a subdivision of a virtual network that specifies a range of IP addresses.

questions.question_text: Which statement is true regarding subnet address space?

options.label: A
options.text: Subnet address space must be a superset of the virtual network address space

options.label: B
options.text: Subnet address space must be a subset of the virtual network address space

options.label: C
options.text: Subnet can use any private IP range regardless of VNet

options.label: D
options.text: Subnet address space cannot overlap with any other subnet in the same VNet

questions.explanation: A subnet's address range must be within the address space of its parent virtual network.

questions.question_text: What is required for two VNets to communicate via VNet peering?

options.label: A
options.text: They must be in the same region

options.label: B
options.text: They must have a shared key

options.label: C
options.text: They must have non-overlapping IP address spaces

options.label: D
options.text: They must be linked via a VPN gateway

questions.explanation: VNet peering requires non-overlapping IP address spaces in the connected virtual networks.

questions.question_text: When peering is established, which traffic flows are enabled by default?
questions.explanation: VNet peering enables bidirectional traffic between the peered virtual networks.

questions.question_text: Which SKU of Public IP is required for a public IP address that can be used with an Azure Load Balancer?
questions.explanation: Only the Standard SKU supports load balancers; Basic SKU is not compatible.

questions.question_text: What happens to the public IP address when the associated VM is deallocated (stop)?

options.label: B
options.text: It remains assigned and retains its configuration

options.label: C
options.text: It changes to a new address

questions.explanation: A public IP address remains allocated to the resource until explicitly released, even if the VM is stopped.

questions.question_text: Which statement about User Defined Routes (UDRs) is true?

options.label: A
options.text: UDRs can only be configured at the subnet level

options.label: B
options.text: UDRs can override the default system routes

options.label: C
options.text: UDRs are applied only to Azure Firewall

options.label: D
options.text: UDRs are not supported in Azure Virtual WAN

questions.explanation: UDRs allow you to specify custom routes that override Azure’s default system routes.

questions.question_text: If two UDRs are defined for the same destination prefix, which factor determines which route is applied?

options.label: A
options.text: The order in which they were created

questions.explanation: UDR priority is determined by the route metric; lower metric routes are applied first.

questions.question_text: Which Azure tool would you use first to verify NSG rules affecting a VM?
questions.explanation: Network Watcher includes features like NSG flow logs and the Connectivity+ test to troubleshoot network issues.

questions.question_text: Which of the following must be verified if VNet peering is not working?

options.label: A
options.text: Both VNets have the same subscription

options.label: B
options.text: Both VNets have non-overlapping IP address spaces

options.label: C
options.text: Both VNets have the same resource group

options.label: D
options.text: Both VNets have the same region

questions.explanation: Peering requires non-overlapping IP address spaces; overlapping ranges prevent traffic flow.
